set.pl: Beside the sec. 27/28 road at the W quarter corner of sec. 27 T2S R7W, Emmett Twp: N. A. Burton's NW¼ (1873 plat), with the Newbre farms across the S-line road
set.st: About 1844 John McArdill, a jewellery pedlar from London, Canada, was robbed of $4,000-5,000. In 1873 an anonymous letter from a former farmhand said he and a partner had hidden the loot in a 40-ft dry well in the Newbre neighbourhood south of the Kalamazoo River, filled in with earth, stones and oak stumps. The well was found on N. A. Burton's lot exactly as described. In Sep 1874 McArdill's party pulled the stumps and dug to 50 ft, reporting nothing. By late October 'the belief has become almost universal' that McArdill got the money on the last day: a neighbour said the diggers had not reached bottom when he went to dinner and were hastily filling the hole when he came back. Pin is the half-mile stake the letter paced from, not the well itself.
pinev: 1873 plat: N. A. Burton 160 = NW¼ sec 27 T2S R7W; Newbre farms across the S-line road; letter's paces put the well within ~120 m of the W quarter corner beside the 27/28 road.
W quarter corner from BLM PLSS (42.26852,-85.12030); the 27/28 road still shows on 2017 Michigan 1 m lidar; dry farmland.

src: Calhoun County atlas (1873), Emmett Twp plate (viewer p. 19, PC (b) read)
